01

Publishing

One markdown file, four outputs

glitu · demo

From one slides.md

  • A standalone page: engine, theme and fonts inside, no network
  • A light page: the engine and the theme come from the web
  • A static site, for any web server
  • An export: editable PowerPoint, vector PDF, PNG images
terminal
glitu build -o talk.html
glitu build --assets https://glitu.net/static
glitu build site -o dist
glitu build pptx -o talk.pptx

glitu build pptx -o talk.pptx

Everything starts from the same markdown file. One page to carry around, which opens with a double click. A light page that loads the engine from glitu.net. A static site, like Hugo. Or an export, for those who need a file.

glitu · demo
02

History

From the desktop to the browser

glitu · demo

PowerPoint opens the story. Beamer turns slides into source code. Keynote. reveal.js brings them to the browser. Slidev writes them in markdown. glitu keeps the markdown and drops npm.

glitu · demo
03

Architecture

The crates, and the diagram tools of your machine

glitu · demo

The markdown goes through glitu; the engine runs it in the browser

Your presentation is plain files. The glitu tool reads them. Its compiler, glitu-core, turns them into slides; the diagrams are drawn by the tools of your machine, skemo first, run confined. glitu-web, compiled to WebAssembly, presents them. What you get. And glitu.net/static hosts each version of the engine and of the themes.

glitu · demo
  • Flowcharts, sequences, states, Gantt
  • Drawn by mermaid.js in a browser glitu drives, or by mmdc
  • A diagram appears as a whole, at its click

Any diagram language glitu knows takes the place of the visual. A Mermaid flowchart, appearing at its click.

glitu · demo
  • Declarative diagrams, by Terrastruct
  • d2.theme=200 and the other declared options on the fence

D2, rendered by the d2 command line of the machine.

glitu · demo
  • The dot command line
  • Graphs laid out automatically

Graphviz, the oldest of them: dot lays the graph out.

Formulas

In LaTeX, rendered at build

glitu · demo

Energy

  • The equivalence E=mc2E = mc^2
  • A sum ∑i=1ni=n(n+1)2\sum_{i=1}^{n} i = \frac{n(n+1)}{2}
∫−∞+∞e−x2dx=π\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} e^{-x^2}\,dx = \sqrt{\pi}

Start with energy. Then Gauss's sum. Finally the integral.

total.rs
fn total(v: &Vec<i32>) -> i32 {
    let mut s = 0;
    for x in v {
        s += x;
    }
    s
}fn total(v: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    let mut s = 0;
    for x in v {
        s += x;
    }
    s
}fn total(v: &[i32]) -> i32 {
    v.iter().sum()
}

One version per click: the words kept slide to their new place.
